svg.title: Annex A1 · Sources, reachability and registry
svg.desc: The official, alert and news sources; the weekly probe that measures their reach from each network and the registry that splits each URL among GitHub Actions, n8n and the Peru machine.
svg.text: Annex A1 · Sources, reachability and registry

What the observatory watches and how it is decided, URL by URL, who fetches it. Every Monday it is measured where each address answers from (GitHub Actions on Azure, n8n on AWS and the machine in Peru) and the registry
assigns each one to a collector. Nobody requests what robots.txt forbids, except 40 news feeds read as a feed reader.

Details these boxes of the full diagram: ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources, NOAA (CPC and PSL), Official hazard alerts (14 sources), Government pages kept from Peru, Media and government: 116 news feeds, Google News: 38 searches, Each
server's robots.txt, Registry builder, Source registry (registry/), Weekly reachability probe.
government feeds and 38 Google News searches
JSON versioned on main; all three collectors follow it

g.title: 1. Each server's robots.txt → Reachability probe: robots.txt first. Before measuring, the probe reads each server's robots.txt. A forbidden path becomes robots-disallowed and is not requested.
2. ENFEN: official communiqué → Reachability probe: Official URLs and mirrors. Every official source URL is measured, including the fallbacks (DHN mirror, IMARPE repository).
3. 13 Peru pages → Reachability probe: archive pages. The daily run does not request the 13 Peru pages (the SENAMHI warning table is read from the Peru copy), but the probe does measure them.
4. 14 alert sources → Reachability probe: alert and news feeds. The 168 feeds are measured the same way: that is how we know which answer from Actions and from n8n.

5. What n8n and Peru measured → reachability.json: n8n and Peru measurements. n8n's latest attempt counts as a measurement of the n8n network; a carried copy counts as its last failure. From Peru, each URL's result and its extra measurements.
6. Reachability probe → reachability.json: Actions measurements. The probe writes what it measured from GitHub Actions, by network and vantage point.
7. reachability.json → Registry builder: all measurements. build_registry runs right after: channels follow the new measurements.
8. Registry builder → sources.json: generates and validates. Writes each URL's status and channels. On main the probe commits registry/; on another branch, to bot/registry/<branch>.
9. Google News: 38 searches → sources.json: exception: 40 reader feeds. Google News, UN News and Sin Rodeos stay with Actions only, as a feed reader: one try, at most every 20 h.
10. sources.json → Who follows it: per-URL channel plan. All three collectors read the same list: each requests only the URLs assigned to it.

ENFEN: official communiqué. Carries the coastal El Niño or La Niña alert status. Portal (WordPress API and /comunicados/ listing) and its mirror at the DHN; IMARPE's repository receives each document about 3 days later. the portal only answers from Peru. Technology: WordPress API, DSpace API, PDF.

g.title: IGP: monthly ICEN. The Coastal El Niño Index as text. Over http it answers everyone; over https only from Peru, like the ENFEN portal. Technology: ICEN.txt.

g.title: NOAA: 15 products. Weekly and monthly OISST, RONI, ONI, SOI, Tahiti and Darwin pressure, 850 hPa winds, heat content, GODAS D20 and the ENSO discussion (CPC); ERSSTv6 Niño 1+2 and 3.4 (PSL). critical: weekly OISST, RONI and ENSO discussion. Technology: texto, HTML, GRIB1.

Tahiti and Darwin pressure, 850 hPa winds,
heat content, GODAS D20 and the ENSO

g.title: IMARPE: weekly bulletin. Subsurface temperature anomaly off Paita and Chicama (BS-OBP), with its quote. Read on Sundays through the IMARPE repository API. Technology: DSpace API, PDF.

g.title: 14 alert sources. INDECI's COEN, SENAMHI (Telegram and 4 ArcGIS layers), NASA FIRMS, USGS, DHN, PTWC and IGP (CENVUL), each in its own format. Technology: RSS, GeoJSON, ArcGIS, CSV, HTML.

g.title: 116 media and government feeds. Government (33, mostly gob.pe searches), national media (14), regional media from 19 departments (27), radio (37) and international (5). Technology: RSS, Atom, JSON Feed, gob.pe.

Google News: 38 searches. By department (25), national (2), world (1) and for outlets without their own feed (10). Their robots.txt forbids them: they are read as a feed reader. at most every 20 h, only from main.

g.title: Each server's robots.txt. Each site's rules for robots, read per RFC 9309: the longest rule wins and, on a tie, Allow. Technology: reach.py.

g.title: Reachability probe. Reads robots.txt and requests every registry URL from Actions. Classifies the answer: ok, 403, 4xx, 5xx, timeout, connection, DNS, TLS, anti-bot check, empty or forbidden. A check is recorded and never bypassed. Mondays 04:17 Lima, by hand or when the probe changes. Technology: probe-sources.yml, probe_sources.py, httpx.

g.title: reachability.json. Every measurement by network (actions, n8n, peru) and vantage point, with class, HTTP code and date. 311 URLs measured from Actions and n8n; none from Peru yet, so no geoblock is confirmed. Technology: JSON.

g.title: Registry builder. Joins the code's catalogs (168 feeds, 17 ENSO sources, 13 Peru pages) with the measurements. Rule: only Peru fetches what is geoblocked; nobody fetches what robots.txt forbids (except 40 reader feeds, Actions only); the rest, Actions and n8n. --check fails if out of date. Technology: build_registry.py, registry.py.

g.title: sources.json. 198 sources and 201 URLs: 152 for Actions and n8n, 40 Actions only (reader) and 9 Peru only. Status: 144 open, 40 forbidden, 9 suspected geoblock, 7 unmeasured and 1 down. committed on main; elsewhere, to bot/registry/. Technology: enso-source-registry/1.
g.text: and n8n, 40 Actions only (reader) and 9 Peru

g.title: Who follows it. GitHub Actions on every run; n8n at 22:50 (from main or its embedded copy); the Peru machine at 21:00 (with its token, or the kit's copy).
